title: Reheating a Frozen Pork Chop (Gentle, Stays Medium-ish)
description: Low-power microwave reheat for a cooked, frozen pork chop. About 10 min. Low power is the whole trick.
steps: Unwrap the chop. Put it on a microwave-safe plate with 1 Tbsp water or broth. Cover with a damp paper towel or a microwave cover.
From frozen: 30% power (or Defrost) for 4 min. Flip. 30% power 3 to 4 min more.
Check the center. Then 50% power in 1-minute bursts until warmed through, about 120 to 130°F in the center for medium-ish.
Let it sit covered 2 min. Season with a little salt.
source: Joe's Meal Pack, Oct 20 to Nov 4, 2026 (built by Thrifty, now kept by Meal Plan), R18
notes:
If thawed in the fridge overnight: skip the defrost step, 50% power 2 to 3 min, flip halfway. More even.
Even quicker and more even: slice the chop thin while partly frozen, then warm the slices at 50% power 1 to 2 min.
Food safety note: USDA recommends reheating leftovers to 165°F. Warming to about 120 to 130°F keeps it medium; that's your call.
Want a crust back? After microwaving, 45 sec per side in a very hot skillet with butter.

healthy: Pork chop gives plenty of protein.
Reheated with water or broth instead of added fat.
not_healthy: Salt and broth add some sodium.
No vegetables or fiber on its own.
